attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his endorsed Substack essay. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: The normalised wording keeps the hedge 'suggests' and the three named properties. It leaves out the 'presumably' clause about benchmarks, but that does not change the core commitment.

contract.note: The contract rightly treats this as a qualified synthesis ('suggests') with no threshold for 'remain elusive'. A plain reading cannot turn hedged language into a firm claim, so no pass or fail condition can be set.

reviews.rationale: The statement is hedged: the evidence 'suggests' the properties remain elusive. 'Elusive' also has no operational threshold. Under policy, hedged language is not scored. The packet has no outcome evidence, and none could settle this without strengthening the claim.

attribution.note: The 'fall short' judgement is Marcus's own. Calling the criteria essential cites Hendrycks et al., a paper Marcus coauthored and endorses here.

semantics.note: This is a faithful, firm observation that current systems fall short on three named criteria. No hedge or horizon is lost.

contract.note: The plain reading requires material weaknesses in all three properties, not error-free performance. That is an ordinary, fair reading. Using the Feb 1–17, 2026 window for 'current systems' is reasonable. The rule that Hendrycks et al. count only as context is correct because Marcus is a coauthor.

evidence.note: The coauthored Hendrycks framework sets out testing criteria, including distribution shifts. Under the contract it shows the criteria only and is not an independent capability finding.

The Feb 3, 2026 International AI Safety Report describes jagged performance and failures on simple tasks. That corroborates weaknesses in general but does not assess each of the three properties separately, and it predates Opus 4.6.
Anthropic's own disclosure of Opus 4.6's long-context gains (Feb 5). It shows progress but not that the three requirements are met.

reviews.rationale: The contract needs independent evaluations showing material weaknesses in all three properties across the frontier of Feb 2026. The safety report gives general corroboration but does not cover each property or the newest models. Opus 4.6's claimed gains do not show the criteria were met. The packet settles neither side.

attribution.note: Marcus wrote this, using 'we' for the essay's authors, and endorses it.

semantics.note: The revised wording restores 'we see no evidence' and 'have tried'. It now matches the source, including its evaluative and self-reporting elements.

contract.note: 'Weakening' is an evaluative judgement with no rule for comparing definitions. 'We see no evidence' reports the authors' own view of the evidence. 'Original standards' has no single operational definition. The contract fairly finds no determinate test.

evidence.note: Legg and Hutter (2007) is a historical formal definition of machine intelligence. It does not supply an agreed threshold for ranking later definitions.
A University of California summary (Feb 5, 2026) of Chen et al.'s competing AGI account. It confirms a redefinition attempt but cannot settle whether that weakens the term.

reviews.rationale: The statement combines an evaluative judgement ('weakening') with the authors' report of their own reading of the evidence ('we see no evidence'). Neither has an operational standard. The evidence documents a competing definition, but it cannot decide whether that definition is weaker or whether the authors' assessment is true.

attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his endorsed essay.

semantics.note: A faithful three-part observation. Shortening 'task formulation, evaluation, and correction' to 'human scaffolding' is acceptable because the contract restores the three functions.

contract.note: Treating the claim as a conjunction with a Feb 2026 window is fair. Reading 'persistent goals' as keeping an assigned objective may understate Marcus's 'self-directed' sense, which the contract flags. Whether assigned-goal benchmarks count against him depends on that choice.

evidence.note: A Feb 2026 preprint finds performance drops as the task horizon grows across five LLM agents. It supports the long-horizon limitation in one restricted environment only.

Anthropic's compiler demonstration documents human-built tests, CI enforcement and repeated regressions. That supports dependence on humans for evaluation and correction. It also shows autonomous task selection, so task formulation is not established.

Andon Labs' Feb 5 benchmark report says the best models sustain performance over thousands of tool calls. That challenges the assigned-goal reading of 'persistent goals', but one structured simulation is not representative.

reviews.rationale: Support requires all three parts. Long-horizon struggles have partial support. Human evaluation and correction are documented in one demonstration, but task formulation and a general lack of persistent goals are not established. Vending-Bench challenges the goal claim, but it is a single structured simulation, not representative evidence. The packet therefore settles neither side.
